gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a named lab measured an SPR AVS profile (9–20 V at up to 5 A) on all three USB-C ports of the Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22, confirmed in practice that it fast-charges an iPhone 18 Pro Max, and measured it keeping 45 W + 45 W with two devices plugged in (techtest.org, Michael Barton, 2026-11-23).
standout_why: I compared against these pages: Apple Support 102574; Charge-Test (iPhone 18 Pro Max, cited in chat 1); ChargerLAB's iPhone 18 Pro review (cited in chat 2), whose English page shows only an intro with no per-charger table; ChargerLAB's iPhone 18 Pro Max review (cited in chat 2); iThinkDifferent (cited in both chats); and zeerawireless (uncited). LTT Labs (cited) returned 403, so I could not compare its text. iThinkDifferent lists the AH22 as AVS-capable from the maker's claim only and has no measurements of its own. Charge-Test's named list has no AH22, ESR or Belkin. ChargerLAB's tables name Apple, CUKTECH, CANDYSIGN, Lenovo, Rewoda and a 'UGREEN 160W'. No rival page gives a measured AVS profile or a measured two-device split for any multi-port charger. The 1-minute AVS advantage on the smaller Pro is only partly new: ChatGPT already quoted LTT saying a non-AVS charger finished 'within a minute or two'.
decides: Apple's 40W Dynamic adapter stays the best-measured pick. On the smaller iPhone 18 Pro, 充电头网 measured it at 17.45 V SPR AVS and 15 min to 50%. On the Pro Max, ChargerLAB measured 51.23 W peak on the compatibility test and 52.9 W peak, 15 min to 50%, on the full-charge test. Our Baseus PicoGo Pro AH22 honestly wins the multi-device segment because a named lab measured its AVS profile on every port and a 45 W + 45 W split. 45 W per port is still above the roughly 42 W the smaller Pro drew on AVS, though 充电头网's peak reading was 45.3 W in another section. That inference comes from comparing two different labs' numbers. Our UGREEN Nexode Air 65W has a named AVS confirmation only on Charge-Test's tested version, and Notebookcheck measured no iPhone. ESR Xtend 45W has only ESR's own lab figure, so it should not enter the top three on measurements. The UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-port has conflicting lab results and should not be featured as an AVS pick unless the exact model is confirmed. On the smaller Pro, the measured AVS advantage over a 15 V PD charger is 1 minute to 50%. The same lab measured full charge 7 minutes slower with AVS (84 vs 77 min). The page should state this honestly.
